blogs.title: Orthogonal Finetuning 101: Intuition Behind Rotating Neurons to Control Diffusion Models
blogs.description: A gentle, non-mathematical introduction to Orthogonal Finetuning (OFT). This post will explain why neuron directions (angles) matter more than magnitudes, how rotating neuron coordinates preserves semantic abilities, and why orthogonality is a sweet spot between flexibility and stability. Targeted at students and tech enthusiasts, it uses visual analogies (Fourier phase vs magnitude, toy autoencoder examples) to build intuition before touching on the core theory.

blogs.title: From Paper to Practice: Implementing OFT on Stable Diffusion (Step-by-Step Guide)
blogs.description: A practical tutorial for ML practitioners showing how to add OFT to a Stable Diffusion finetuning pipeline. Covers which layers to target (attention vs conv), block-diagonal Cayley parameterization, initialization, enforcing orthogonality, training tips (learning rate, block size r), and how to fold the learned orthogonal matrix into weights at inference time. Includes guidance on reproducing DreamBooth-style subject-driven and ControlNet-style controllable generation experiments.

blogs.title: OFT vs LoRA vs ControlNet: Which Finetuning Tool Should You Use?
blogs.description: A comparative analysis aimed at engineers deciding on a finetuning approach. This article breaks down strengths and trade-offs: parameter efficiency, convergence speed, stability, inference overhead, expressiveness, and typical failure modes. It uses empirical takeaways from the paper (convergence and control consistency) and provides decision heuristics (when to prefer OFT or COFT, when adapters or low-rank updates still make sense).

blogs.title: Measuring What Matters: Hyperspherical Energy and Why It Predicts Semantic Preservation
blogs.description: An explainer for ML researchers and advanced students on hyperspherical energy—what it measures, why pairwise neuron angles encode semantic structure, and why preserving this energy helps avoid catastrophic finetuning changes. The post will show how to compute HE on real layers, visualize changes during finetuning, and use HE as a diagnostic for safe model adaptation.

blogs.title: Constrained OFT (COFT) and Re-scaled OFT: Making Finetuning Stable and Flexible
blogs.description: A focused walkthrough of COFT and re-scaled OFT variants that add radius constraints or per-neuron scaling to balance flexibility and stability. The post explains the epsilon-deviation constraint, projected updates on the Cayley parameters, and when to use re-scaling. Practical recommendations for hyperparameters and examples of how these variants reduce collapse in subject-driven and control tasks are included.

blogs.title: Designing Control Consistency Metrics for Controllable Generation
blogs.description: A practical guide to evaluating controllable text-to-image models, inspired by the paper's new metric. It describes approaches to recover control signals from generated images (edge detectors, segmentation models, landmark regressors), how to compute IoU/F1/landmark L2 metrics, and pitfalls when interpreting results. Useful for practitioners running benchmarks or ablation studies.

blogs.title: Advanced Topics: Efficient Orthogonal Parameterizations and Scaling OFT
blogs.description: A technical deep-dive for ML engineers and researchers into implementation choices that affect scalability: Cayley transform details, block-diagonal vs shared blocks, Neumann-series approximations, matrix inverse costs, and potential GPU/FP16 gotchas. The post also surveys possible optimizations (sparse/sketching, structured orthogonality) and open engineering problems mentioned in the paper.

blogs.title: Future Directions: Compositional Finetuning, Multi-task OFT, and Ethical Considerations
blogs.description: A forward-looking post exploring open problems and broader impacts. Topics include composing orthogonal matrices from multiple tasks (can one model remember many finetunings?), combining OFT with parameter-efficient methods, implications for personalization and misuse (privacy, deepfakes), and research opportunities to improve parameter-efficiency without biasing flexibility.
